fixes.explanation: He sure does. As soon as Jacob sees Rachel with Laban's sheep, he goes up, rolls the stone away from the mouth of the well, and waters his uncle's sheep (Genesis 29:10). Just before this, the shepherds told him, “We cannot, until all the flocks have been gathered and the stone has been rolled away…” (Genesis 29:8). Then Jacob walks up and rolls it himself, like that stone owed him money!

Right, he stays. Jacob finishes the week's celebration, and Laban gives him Rachel as his wife (Genesis 29:28). Then the text says he worked for Laban another seven years (Genesis 29:30). Nobody packs a bag in this passage, friend. Seven more years is a LONG time to wait, and I think that tells you how much he loved her.

Careful, friend, that one is False. When Jacob asks if they know Laban the grandson of Nahor, the shepherds answer, “We know him…” (Genesis 29:5). Then Jacob asks, “Is he well?” and they say, “Yes,” and point out that Laban's daughter Rachel is coming with his sheep (Genesis 29:6). Jacob asked one little question and got good news AND Rachel walking up. That's a bonus nobody ordered!

Nope, no asking him to wait in this story, friend. Once Jacob tells her he's Rebekah's son and a relative of her father, the text says she ran and told her father (Genesis 29:12). Ran! If somebody told me a relative of my father was standing at the well, I'd be moving too. I'd trip over my own apron, but I'd be moving.

Isaac doesn't come up in Laban's reply, friend. Laban says, “Better that I give her to you than to another. Stay here with me.” (Genesis 29:19) No stopping to make a call, no "let me get back to you." Laban says it's better to give Rachel to Jacob than to another, and then he tells Jacob to stay. I think Laban had made up his mind.

Isaac's flocks never come up here, friend. Laban says they will give Jacob the younger one in return for another seven years of work (Genesis 29:27). What Laban asks for is more of Jacob's work. Seven years was already a long stretch, and now he asks for seven more. I'd need a bigger calendar.

problems.problem: It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
The joke says Jacob got a daughter, but Rachel was Laban's daughter. The image is confusing rather than a clear joke.
The text does not say the stone had been sitting there all day.
The text does not say the shepherds were the only ones waiting at the well.
Papa's hypothetical refers to his father, inventing another family member.
The explanation is flat and repeats Laban's answer without much of Papa's personality.
The passage does not identify Jacob's seven years of work as sheep tending, or state that no flocks changed hands.
The reference to Papa being stuck lacks the drawer context. The comparison also does not fit Jacob accepting the deal.
